title: Explainable and Context-Aware Financial Nudges via Event-Driven Microservices
venue: International Journal of Emerging Research in Engineering and Technology
tldr: Presents a modular, event-driven microservices framework that integrates SHAP-based explainable AI to deliver context-aware, transparent financial nudges in real-time fintech applications.
problem_and_motivation: Existing financial notification systems often deliver generic, opaque alerts that fail to engage users or build trust. There is a significant gap in integrating real-time context, explainability, and modular scalability into a single financial advisory system.
approach: Proposes a Kafka-based microservices architecture with five modular services: Data Ingestor, Context Processor, Nudge Decision Engine, XAI Module, and Notification Service.
Ingests multi-modal data streams including transactions, user behavior signals, and opt-in geolocation via open banking APIs.
Enriches events with historical behavior, budget goals, temporal patterns, and location context to create a holistic user snapshot.
Uses a Nudge Decision Engine with rule-based logic or a trained ML model to classify events as 'nudge-worthy'.
Integrates a SHAP-based XAI module that generates feature attributions and converts them into human-readable, templated explanations.
Evaluates the framework on synthetic and anonymized financial datasets to simulate diverse user behaviors.
Implements performance optimizations like caching, fast SHAP variants, and asynchronous explanation generation via Kafka.
Adheres to security and privacy principles including OAuth 2.0, TLS encryption, RBAC, and user consent management.
findings: num: Contextual triggers (e.g., time, location, prior habits) are effective in increasing user engagement.
num: Explainability boosts users' perceived relevance and trust in the system.
The proposed framework bridges the gap between intelligent personalization and transparent automation in fintech.
SHAP provides local interpretability with formal guarantees of fairness, consistency, and local accuracy.
The microservices architecture ensures modularity, fault isolation, and data minimization for privacy-sensitive environments.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a novel applied framework that integrates event-driven microservices, machine learning, and explainable AI for real-time financial nudging. It addresses the gap between personalization and transparency in fintech by embedding SHAP-based explanations directly into a modular, scalable pipeline. The architecture provides a practical blueprint for deploying ethical, user-centered financial advisory systems that prioritize trust, privacy, and regulatory compliance. By combining Kafka's event streaming with XAI, it demonstrates a path toward more interpretable and auditable automated financial advice.
directly_justifies: Contextual triggers like time, location, and prior habits effectively increase user engagement.
Explainability boosts users' perceived relevance and trust in the system.
The architecture adheres to principles of modularity, fault isolation, and data minimization.
SHAP provides local interpretability with formal guarantees of fairness, consistency, and local accuracy.
limits: The system is evaluated only on synthetic and anonymized datasets, not real-world user data.
The specific ML model used for classification is not identified or detailed.
Real-world effectiveness of nudges and explanations requires behavioral A/B testing.
Computational cost of SHAP in real-time applications is acknowledged but not fully addressed.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: A systematic scan across all topic domains was performed. The paper is highly relevant to domains concerning budgeting (7.A, 7.B), user trust and privacy (10.A, 10.B, 10.C), and engagement (11.A, 11.B). It has medium relevance to predictive modeling (6.A), anomaly detection (8.A), and algorithm evaluation (12.B) as these are components of the proposed system. Domains like culturally specific financial practices (2.A, 2.B, 2.C, 2.D) and savings/debt management (13.A, 13.B, 13.C) were rejected as the paper does not focus on these specific Filipino or user-declared contexts. The topic codes selected reflect the paper's core contributions to modular, explainable, and secure real-time financial advisory systems.
